subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: What bounded retention contract should cron quarantine recovery use when repeated sidecar overflows occur?
rationale: The correct tradeoff between retaining prior quarantined records and preventing local disk exhaustion is a persistent-data policy choice; the current unique-file approach makes that choice implicitly and without a bound.

options.title: Bound retained archives
options.body: Keep a small fixed count or byte budget of recent recovery archives, delete older ones deterministically, and add regression coverage for repeated overflows.

options.title: Fail closed after one archive
options.body: Preserve one recovery artifact and reject later cap-overflow writes until an operator resolves the invalid cron entries.

options.title: Accept indefinite archives
options.body: Document that every overflow permanently creates a new archive and accept the resulting disk-growth risk.

recommendation.title: Bound retained archives
recommendation.body: Keep a small fixed count or byte budget of recent recovery archives, delete older ones deterministically, and add regression coverage for repeated overflows.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR directly asks for a maintainer decision on a core runtime-hardening and persisted-state behavior; Vincent Koc is the strongest available review-routing signal in the supplied context.
